# Back matter

Not the last chapter of the book, and carrying no placement marker: it grows no
index section as the fixture stands. It is the chapter a placement marker is
appended to when a check needs a marker to appear between two renders, and the
chapter whose store path a check holds with a directory when it needs a record
that can never be written — both a chapter ahead of the one that reports.

A second term for the index no marker names: [Dovetail]{.index index="gamma"}.

The six mark forms below are what makes this chapter's recovery worth fencing:
a chapter read back from its own source has to reach every shape an author
writes, not only the bare mark above. Each is on a term no other mark in this
book indexes, because the sort-key registry is keyed on the printed level path
and a term marked in two chapters would put two chapters' keys in question (the
M13 lesson, extended M56).

More than one level, so recovery has to rebuild a sub-entry and the parent it
hangs under: [joinery]{.index entry="Woodwork!Joinery" index="gamma"}.

A declared sort key, which is a value the author wrote rather than a conclusion
this chapter reached, so recovery carries it: [Zephyr]{.index index="gamma"
sort="Abacus"}.

A cross-reference sending the reader somewhere else instead of listing a page,
whose target is a term five.qmd marks: [Ferrule]{.index index="gamma"
see="Escutcheon"}.

A cross-reference sending the reader somewhere else as well — which in this
extension still prints no page of its own: [Hasp]{.index index="gamma"
see-also="Escutcheon"}.

A range that opens [Ingot]{.index index="gamma" range="open"} here and closes
[Ingot]{.index index="gamma" range="close"} here. Nothing outside this
chapter's own process pairs it, so a recovered pair indexes as though the
attribute were absent.

Which occurrence is the proper one, a role no other process resolved for a
recovered mark: [Jetty]{.index index="gamma" mention="principal"}.
